legend.purpose: Section names screen-printed on the panel. Replaces h1 outside rendered note content.

headline.purpose: h2 inside rendered content and on document-shaped surfaces.

title.purpose: A rack unit's name, lifted from the note's first block. Single line, ellipsized.

body.purpose: Rendered note prose in the preview bay, capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: Key faces, nav switches, and control legends. Tracked uppercase.

signal.purpose: Anything literal or measured: filenames, paths, dates, counts, tags.

subhead.purpose: h3 in rendered content, and the one large readout value on a stat tile.

source.purpose: The editor's own text. One step up from signal, because it is read for minutes rather than glanced at.

field.purpose: Text the user is typing into a patch field.

note.purpose: Secondary panel text still meant to be read: vault paths, result first lines, backlinks, doctor references.

micro.purpose: The smallest screen-printed legend. Section labels, small keys, readout tracks, tags.

nano.purpose: A legend that sits inside a row without competing with it: category chips, editor head category.

shadows.name: inset-well
shadows.purpose: A recess milled into the panel. Dark at the top lip, catch-light along the bottom.

shadows.name: key-face
shadows.purpose: A capped button standing proud of the panel.

shadows.name: cap-edge
shadows.purpose: The anodized category cap's machined edges.

shadows.name: lamp-glow
shadows.purpose: The only glow in the system. Indicator lamps only.

shadows.name: engraved-rule
shadows.purpose: Paired with a 1px engrave border to read as a groove rather than a line.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Genuine overlays that leave the panel plane: modals, popovers, combobox lists.

narrative.overview:
Yak Shears is an instrument you operate at speed, so the interface is a console panel rather than a page of documents. It refuses the arrangement every note app ships: a grey sidebar tree beside a white document pane, with every note drawn as an identical card. The vault is a rack of channel strips, one unit per note, each with its category cap, its four lines of note, and its readout in the same place. You sweep the readout column, throw a switch, and work in the center section.

Three materials do all the structural work and every component is built from them. The panel is the painted face things are mounted on. The well is a recess milled into it, where content and inputs sit down. The engrave is a groove cut into the panel, drawn as a dark line over a lighter one so it reads as cut rather than as a stroked border. On top of the materials sit the parts: screen-printed legends, anodized caps carrying category color, and indicator lamps that report state in size as well as color.

The panel is anodized charcoal, slightly blue rather than neutral, with a fine directional grain instead of a flat fill. This matters because a flat neutral grey is the timid rendition of this world and it takes the life out of every cap and lamp mounted on it. Both color schemes are real consoles: light is a painted panel under daylight, dark is the same desk at night. Neither is an inversion of the other, and neither turns the instrument into paper.
keyCharacteristics: Three materials (panel, well, engrave) compose every component; nothing is a floating card
Amber is the only lit color in the chrome and it means armed
Category color owns whole rows, not slivers
Depth is machined, not ambient: insets and catch-lights, no drop shadows on the panel
Screen-printed sans for chrome, monospace for anything literal or measured
Hardware travel is 1px; controls move a little, not a lot

rules.name: The Lamps-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, red, and amber appear as state and never as decoration. A lamp answers a question about the system right now; if nothing is being reported, no lamp lights.

rules.name: The One Armed Key Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the action that will fire, so exactly one primary key belongs in any control group. A full-width slab of amber on a control that is always present spends the panel's only lit color on nothing.

rules.name: The Unlit-Off-Limits Rule
rules.body: --lamp-off (#464d55) is for hardware that is dark, never for text. Dim text steps down to --legend-dim, which stays above the contrast floor.

rules.name: The Legend-Never-Content Rule
rules.body: A legend names a control. It never carries the note. Panel heading styles are scoped away from rendered content, because a heading the user wrote is theirs and stays a heading.

rules.name: The Tabular Column Rule
rules.body: Anything that appears at the same position on consecutive rows takes font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Counts and dates in a rack must line up on the digit or the readout column stops being a column.

rules.name: The Row-Pitch Rule
rules.body: Every rack unit is exactly one rack height. Content never sets the row height.

rules.name: The dvh Rule
rules.body: dvh, never vh. overflow-x: clip, never hidden, because hidden stops the sticky header from sticking.

rules.name: The Machined-Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth is stated by inset and catch-light, not by a blur under the element. If a surface is on the panel, it casts no shadow onto it.

rules.name: The Engraved-Pair Rule
rules.body: A division is a 1px solid --engrave over a 1px solid --engrave-light. A single grey line is a border; the pair is a groove.

rules.name: The No-Side-Bar Rule
rules.body: State is never communicated by a colored border down one edge of a row. That vocabulary belongs to the category cap, which means identity. Severity uses lamps; selection uses the seated well plus the lit underline.

dos: Do build new surfaces from the three materials. Ask whether the thing is recessed, flush, or proud, and use --inset-well, the panel face, or the key shadow accordingly.
Do put --anodize under any large panel surface. A flat fill is what made the first rendition read as dated.
Do reserve amber for the armed action and the seated position of latched controls.
Do use lamps (7px circle plus 55% glow) for state, and the category cap for identity.
Do set anything literal or measured in --font-signal with tabular figures, and anything that labels a control in tracked uppercase sans.
Do give repeating rows a fixed height and fixed readout tracks so the column can be swept in one pass.
Do read the layout tokens (--header-height, --action-bar-height, --tap-target, --keyboard-inset, --safe-*) instead of hardcoding a value one of them already names.
Do pair every engraved division with its catch-light.
donts: Don't mark state with a colored border down one side of a row. Lamps for severity, seated well plus lit underline for selection.
Don't cast a drop shadow onto the panel. Only genuine overlays (modals, popovers) leave the panel plane.
Don't use --lamp-off for text; it sits near 2:1 on the panel. Dim text is --legend-dim.
Don't let a lit color decorate. If it is not reporting state or arming an action, it is not lit.
Don't style rendered note content with panel chrome. Scope panel heading and legend rules away from .preview-content, .card__preview, and .search-preview.
Don't animate width or height for a fill or a reveal. Clip it.
Don't make the light scheme white. Both schemes are the same instrument under different room light.
Don't ship a rule no page exercises. There is no build step to tree-shake, the asset budget is 14KB, and the e2e suite fails below 90% CSS rule coverage.
